status: Draft for expert review. Not yet validated. Thresholds were written before any lecture was scored with this version.
scale: Each criterion is scored 0, 1 or 2. Level 2 requires the specific behaviour named, not general competence. Results are reported as a profile per dimension, with no single total.

flags.name: Content error
flags.rule: Any factual or technical error stated and not corrected later in the lecture. Reported with its timestamp; not scored.

descriptive.name: Time per learning objective
descriptive.rule: Minutes of lecture spent on each stated objective, from timestamps. Reported, not scored.

dimensions.name: Topic coverage and depth relative to learning objectives

levels.0: Not addressed, or mentioned only in passing (a single mention or under one minute).
levels.1: Explained: defined and followed by at least one sentence of explanation.
levels.2: Developed: explained, tied to an example or demonstration, and at least one misconception, edge case or limitation is discussed.

levels.0: Fewer than half of the stated objectives reach level 1 on TC1.
levels.2: All reach level 1 and at least half reach level 2.

levels.1: Concrete examples for fewer than half of the objectives.
levels.2: Concrete examples for at least half of the objectives.

levels.1: At least one example is worked through step by step.
levels.2: At least one worked example is also checked or varied: the result is verified, an input is changed, or a counterexample is shown.
Three or more kinds (everyday analogy, numeric case, code, diagram, counterexample).

levels.0: No code, derivation or diagram is shown.
levels.1: Shown only as finished material on slides.
levels.2: Built live during the lecture: typed, written or drawn on screen or board.

levels.1: Run or checked once, with the result visible on screen.
levels.2: Result compared against an expectation stated beforehand, or an error deliberately triggered and then fixed.

levels.0: The demonstration is not linked to the concept being taught.
levels.2: The instructor points to specific lines, steps or parts and says which concept each one implements.

levels.0: No statement of topic or goals.
levels.1: Topic stated at the start or summarised at the end.
levels.2: Objectives stated at the start and revisited in a closing summary.

levels.0: A concept is used before it is introduced.
levels.1: Concepts appear in a workable order without explicit links.
levels.2: New ideas are explicitly connected to ones already covered.

levels.1: Questions asked but not answered by students, or rhetorical only.
levels.2: Questions answered by students, or an in-class exercise.
